original_abstract.text: Dynamic Sparse Training (DST) periodically prunes and regrows connections, inducing a discrete dynamical mechanism over network topologies. At extreme sparsity ($\ge 99\%$), this dynamic tends to destroy input-output information pathways, and performance with standard magnitude/random updates degrades sharply. We formalize forward, backward, and functional reachability on layered sparse graphs, derive closed-form expectations for reachable neurons and edges, and show that Monte Carlo realizations match the theory. Guided by this reachability-based structure, we bias pruning toward non-functional edges and regrowth toward functionally consistent candidates. We introduce this reachability-driven modification of topology evolution as Reachability-guided in DST, referred to as guided DST. On CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny ImageNet, guided DST recovers large accuracy gaps versus unguided DST (up to $+14.4$ points at $99.9\%$ sparsity on CIFAR-100), and on MLP-Mixer guided DST remains trainable at $99.99\%$ sparsity while unguided random regrowth degrades sharply. These results cast extreme-sparse training as a connectivity-preserving dynamical process. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/mzjaworski/ea_dst.
original_abstract.source_title: When Sparsity Breaks Connectivity: Functional Reachability and Guided Topology Dynamics in Extreme Sparse Training

en.text: The paper connects extreme dynamic-sparse-training failure to broken input–output pathways and guides pruning/regrowth using functional reachability. On image benchmarks it recovers up to 14.4 accuracy points at 99.9% sparsity; an MLP-Mixer remains trainable at 99.99% sparsity where unguided regrowth degrades. Connectivity-preserving sparse training may inform recommendation architectures, but the evidence is from vision tasks.

zh.text: 极端稀疏训练中，剪枝与重新生长可能切断输入到输出的信息通路。该研究按功能可达性引导连接删除和恢复，在图像基准中，99.9%稀疏率下最高恢复14.4个百分点准确率；MLP-Mixer在99.99%稀疏率下仍可训练。保持连通性的思路可供稀疏推荐模型参考，目前证据来自视觉任务。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval is known for its efficient end-to-end indexing and retrieval. In particular, numeric Document Identifiers (DocIDs) are generally more efficient because they are shorter and generally fixed-length sequences over a small vocabulary, requiring fewer decoding steps during beam search. However, they tend to generalize poorly to unseen documents and must be learned during indexing-stage training. In this paper, we propose a numeric DocID design for generative retrieval that enables better adaptation to unseen documents without retraining. Our DocID design inherits the language model's knowledge: each DocID is a sequence of tokens factorized into bits, and each token is scored as the sum of its bits. Unlike existing numeric DocIDs, whose tokens carry meaning only through embeddings memorized during indexing training, each bit here derives its meaning from the model's representation. Therefore, the DocIDs of unseen documents remain scorable without retraining. Experiments on three benchmarks show that our DocID design substantially improves unseen-document retrieval while maintaining comparable performance on seen documents. It achieves over 20 percentage points higher Hit@10 on unseen documents and up to 7 times lower inference latency than existing numeric DocID designs on NQ320K and TriviaQA, while performing only 3 percentage points below weight-update methods on MS MARCO without additional training. These results show that an appropriate DocID design can heavily reduce retraining costs when adapting generative retrievers to new documents.
original_abstract.source_title: Computed, not Memorized: Bit-Factorized Identifiers for Efficient Generative Retrieval

en.text: This generative-retrieval design factorizes numeric document identifiers into bits whose scores derive from the language model's representations, allowing new documents to remain scorable without retraining identifier embeddings. Across three benchmarks it improves unseen-document retrieval while maintaining comparable seen-document results; reported latency comparisons concern numeric-ID baselines. The approach is relevant to reducing index-refresh training costs in dynamic retrieval systems, with transfer to recommendation still untested.

zh.text: 该生成式检索方法将数字文档ID拆成若干比特，并从语言模型表示计算比特得分，使新文档无需重训ID嵌入也能被打分。三个基准中，未见文档检索改善，已见文档效果保持可比；论文的延迟比较针对数字ID基线。其可借鉴之处是降低动态检索的索引更新训练成本，向推荐任务迁移仍需验证。

original_abstract.text: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. Our Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes, together with published Llama-style experiments, show that our law predicts loss with up to $11\times$ lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. Finally, we extend our law to layer-wise mixed precision and identify the optimal quantized-pretraining recipe, i.e., model size, training tokens, and per-layer forward/backward precision, under a hardware-aware compute budget. Unlike prior precision scaling laws, our law predicts that the optimal precision increases with the compute budget.
original_abstract.source_title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining

en.text: This mixed-precision scaling law separates capacity loss from persistent optimization error in forward and backward quantization. Selected 4-bit Qwen3 experiments and published Llama-style results yield up to 11× lower loss-prediction MSE than prior laws. A hardware-aware cost model jointly chooses model size, tokens and layer-wise precision, predicting higher optimal precision at larger budgets. This informs possible ranking-training budget studies, not demonstrated CTR gains or measured end-to-end acceleration.

zh.text: 该混合精度缩放律区分量化造成的容量损失与前向、反向持续优化误差。在所选 4-bit Qwen3 实验及已发表的 Llama 风格实验上，损失预测 MSE 相比既有规律最低约为后者的 1/11。其硬件感知成本模型联合选择模型规模、token 数与逐层精度，并预测预算增大时最优精度升高。对排序训练预算研究仅有方法启发，不代表 CTR 收益或端到端实测加速。

original_abstract.text: A recommendation request on Reddit draws several replies, each naming different titles. When an LLM recommender is trained on such threads with reinforcement learning (RL), which replies should a generated list be rewarded against? The state-of-the-art recipe, Rank-GRPO, picks one reply per training example, so the advantage mostly records which reply was drawn (85% of its variance) rather than how good the list is. We argue that RL should train on the request, not on each answer, and propose ReMaRk: it scores every list once against the union of all replies' titles and samples each request equally. This makes RL cheaper. On seven backbones and three datasets, ReMaRk reaches the validation recall of 2,000 per-reply RL steps in 25 to 53% of the steps and leads at that budget; trained until neither improves, it is never significantly behind Rank-GRPO and in four of seven pairs reaches Rank-GRPO's best with fewer GPU-hours. The same reward helps on ProtoQA, where about 100 people answer each question, which points to a simple rule for RL with several valid human answers: reward them jointly.
original_abstract.source_title: Many Right Answers, One Training Example: Removing Responder Noise from GRPO for LLM Recommenders

en.text: When a recommendation request has several valid human replies, rewarding each generated list against one sampled reply adds responder noise. ReMaRk instead scores the list against the union of titles across replies and samples requests uniformly. Across seven backbones and three datasets, it reaches the validation recall of 2000 per-reply RL steps in 25–53% of those steps. In longer runs it is never significantly behind Rank-GRPO, but only four of seven pairs reach that baseline's best result with fewer GPU-hours. The evidence concerns LLM recommendation training, not online CTR gains.

zh.text: 一个推荐请求往往有多个人工回答；若每次只随机选一个回答评价生成列表，奖励会混入回答者差异造成的噪声。ReMaRk 按请求均匀采样，并以所有回答中的物品名称并集统一评分。在七个基座模型、三个数据集上，达到按回答训练基线 2000 步时的验证召回水平，仅需其 25–53% 的步数。更长训练中，其结果没有显著落后于 Rank-GRPO，但只有七组对比中的四组以更少 GPU 小时达到该基线的最佳结果。证据针对语言模型推荐训练，不代表线上 CTR 收益。

original_abstract.text: Long-context training of large language and multimodal models couples structured attention masks (document, prefix-LM, share-question, sliding-window, block-sparse) with multi-node context parallelism, making the mask a dominant bottleneck. FlashMask's column-wise sparse mask compresses them from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n)$ via four query-axis boundary vectors, covering broad structured patterns. Implemented for Ampere GPUs, it neither exploits FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA warp-specialized pipeline on Hopper nor supports distribution. The column-wise sparse mask is indexed by key positions but stores query-axis interval boundaries. Under any multi-chunk context-parallel assignment, it reduces per-rank mask localization to a provably zero-communication \emph{clip--shift--max} on the boundary vectors, compatible with the single-GPU kernel. FlashMask-3 introduces a mask-aware Hopper kernel with three-role warp specialization atop FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA pipeline, plus a mask-aware distributed extension: zero-communication mask localization, a sparsity-aware load balancer (HCC-IPO), and a mask-aware compute-communication overlap with mask-driven communication pruning, whose forward all-gather uses topology-aware hierarchical routing. On a single H100 across 12 masks at 4K--128K context, it improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask, FlexAttention, and MagiAttention by 45--141%, 34--71%, and 2--44%. At context-parallel degrees 4--32 with 8K sequence per device, it attains 31--75% compute-communication overlap efficiency and improves throughput over Megatron-Core CP ring, Megatron-Core CP all-gather, and MagiAttention by $1.80\times$--$3.71\times$, $1.71\times$--$2.92\times$, and $1.09\times$--$1.46\times$. In end-to-end training of a 118B-A14B MoE at 128K on 128 H100 GPUs, it raises throughput by 7.3--11.0% over a Dual Chunk all-gather baseline, with attention forward+backward 24.5--44.9% faster.
original_abstract.source_title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention

en.text: FlashMask-3 combines a Hopper-optimized structured-mask attention kernel with zero-communication mask localization, load balancing and communication pruning for context parallelism. In 118B-A14B MoE training at 128K context on 128 H100 GPUs, throughput improves 7.3–11.0% over Dual Chunk all-gather. The separate kernel and distributed-attention gains are not end-to-end gains. Long-sequence ranking may benefit from these systems ideas, subject to mask and hardware compatibility; CTR transfer is untested.

zh.text: FlashMask-3 将 Hopper 优化的结构化掩码注意力核与零通信掩码本地化、负载均衡及通信裁剪结合。在 128 张 H100 上训练 128K 上下文的 118B-A14B MoE 时，相比 Dual Chunk all-gather，端到端吞吐提升 7.3–11.0%；独立核和分布式注意力的更大收益不能混为端到端收益。其对长序列排序仅有系统实现启发，需满足掩码与硬件条件，未验证 CTR。

original_abstract.text: The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank $I + AB^\top$ residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.
original_abstract.source_title: Virtual Head Attention

en.text: Virtual Head Attention uses linear query premixing and low-rank head postmixing that fold into standard GQA-2 at inference. Across four 50B-token pretraining scales, it reports better evaluated quality with smaller KV caches; the dense comparisons use GQA-8 and the MoE comparison GQA-4. A separate matched long-context MoE study reduces KV heads only in full-attention layers. Its cache/quality tradeoff suggests ranking-attention designs, but no CTR results establish benefit.

zh.text: Virtual Head Attention 通过线性 query 预混合与低秩头后混合，在推理时折叠为标准 GQA-2。四档规模、50B-token 预训练比较中，其评测质量改善且 KV 缓存更小；稠密模型对照为 GQA-8，MoE 对照为 GQA-4。另一组匹配的长上下文 MoE 实验仅减少全注意力层的 KV 头，不能推为全模型缓存减半。其缓存与质量权衡可启发排序注意力设计，但未验证 CTR 收益。

original_abstract.text: Long-context inference makes the key-value (KV) cache a major memory bottleneck for large language models. We propose BELT, a low-rank KV cache compression framework. Its key-side objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys or pre-softmax logits, yielding a quadratic surrogate with a closed-form low-rank solution. A learned global rank allocator uses differentiable soft selection during training and hard selection at deployment to meet a user-specified component budget. Experiments demonstrate improved model quality under aggressive compression and increased decoding throughput at comparable accuracy. Evaluated across three LLMs and multiple benchmarks, BELT achieves up to 70% low-rank KV cache compression while outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 23.3 points on LongBench, and up to 17.8x overall KV cache reduction when combined with quantization. With Triton-based GPU kernels and a quantized cache, BELT delivers up to 2.7x speedup for the attention module and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput.
original_abstract.source_title: BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation

en.text: BELT compresses KV caches using an attention-distribution-based low-rank objective and a learned global rank allocator under a component budget. Across three LLMs, the authors report up to 70% low-rank cache compression and benchmark-specific gains; combining quantization reaches up to 17.8x cache reduction. GPU kernels yield up to 2.7x attention speedup and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput. These maxima describe different evaluated configurations; recommendation transfer remains untested.

zh.text: BELT按注意力分布的变化来选择KV缓存的低秩近似，并在固定预算下学习各部分的秩分配。三个语言模型实验报告最高70%的低秩缓存压缩，结合量化最高达到17.8倍缓存缩减；GPU实现最高提升2.7倍注意力速度和3.3倍端到端解码吞吐。这些最大值来自不同测试配置，推荐场景收益尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: Long-running agents retain KV caches across turns and sessions for hours or days. Compressing these persistent caches requires reducing storage while controlling reconstruction error. We present AlignPred, a codec that combines local alignment with predictive coding under a configurable KV reconstruction-error budget. Local orthogonal transforms align related heads or layers into a common coordinate frame, allowing AlignPred to combine token-wise prediction with same-token prediction across heads or layers. Residuals are quantized on an error-bounded lattice and entropy-coded, without learned predictors, encoder-side mode search, or large joint transforms. Across three attention mechanisms, AlignPred requires less storage than the evaluated baselines at comparable measured reconstruction error. Against the evaluated CPU codec implementations, it decodes at least 1.6 times faster while matching or improving encode time. AlignPred achieves near-native task scores at substantially compressed operating points on LongBench-Pro at 128K context. AlignPred's SGLang HiCache integration reduces persistent target-KV storage by 42-72% relative to native HiCache, with comparable latency.
original_abstract.source_title: AlignPred: Error-Controlled KV Cache Compression via Alignment and Predictive Coding

en.text: AlignPred compresses persistent KV caches using local orthogonal alignment, cross-token/head/layer prediction and error-bounded residual coding. Its SGLang HiCache integration reduces persistent target-KV storage by 42–72% relative to native HiCache at comparable latency. It also preserves near-native scores at tested 128K LongBench-Pro operating points. The result concerns persistent cache storage; recommendation transfer remains untested.

zh.text: 长期运行的智能体需要持续保存KV缓存。AlignPred先对齐相关头或层，再预测并编码残差，以可配置误差预算控制重建质量。接入SGLang HiCache后，持久化目标KV存储减少42%—72%，延迟相当；在128K LongBench-Pro测试配置中也保持接近原生的分数。该结果针对持久缓存，推荐应用尚待验证。

original_abstract.text: On-policy self-distillation improves a model using guidance from the model itself, but it still requires a teacher that provides more useful predictions than the student. Existing approaches obtain such guidance by giving the teacher additional context or instructions. We ask whether it can instead come from changing how the same model uses its own layers. To address this, we introduce LoOPSD, which searches over a model's layer execution order to construct a stronger teacher and distills its advantage into the student. Specifically, we keep the model weights unchanged while searching for layers to repeat, and use the resulting teacher's predictions on student-generated prefixes to guide learning. We then alternate search and distillation, rebuilding the teacher from the updated student in each round so that the student progressively absorbs the gains from alternative layer execution. Experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning tasks show improvements across models. On GSM8K with a 400-token thinking budget, LoOPSD raises Qwen3-1.7B accuracy from 42.30% to 79.61%; subsequent distillation rounds yield further gains beyond the first round. Together, these findings show that by searching layer execution to construct teachers, we can turn a model's additional computation into improved student capabilities, opening a new avenue for self-distillation to derive supervision from the model's own computation.
original_abstract.source_title: LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers

en.text: LoOPSD searches for beneficial layer repetitions while holding weights fixed, uses the resulting stronger looped teacher to guide on-policy self-distillation, then repeats search and distillation. On GSM8K at a 400-token thinking budget, Qwen3-1.7B accuracy increases from 42.30% to 79.61%; later rounds add gains. The method offers a way to distill extra computation into a student, with recommendation transfer untested.

zh.text: 自蒸馏需要比学生更有用的教师信号。LoOPSD保持权重不变，搜索哪些层值得重复执行，形成更强的循环教师，再用学生自己生成的轨迹进行蒸馏，并交替重复这两步。在400词元思考预算的GSM8K实验中，Qwen3-1.7B准确率由42.30%升至79.61%。该方法可研究如何把额外计算转移到学生能力中，推荐效果尚未验证。

original_abstract.text:
Large-scale expert parallelism (EP) has become the standard deployment configuration for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models in production. Meanwhile, the highly dynamic nature of LLM workloads requires providers to continuously adjust serving capacity to match fluctuating demand. Scaling MoE serving cannot be efficiently achieved by simply adding or removing serving instances; instead, it often requires resizing the EP group within an existing instance, which we refer to as intra-instance scaling.Existing inference engines primarily rely on instance-level scaling, which destroys and reconstructs entire serving instances, incurring substantial scaling overhead.
  We present FastEEP (Fast Elastic Expert Parallel), a fast intra-instance scaling system for MoE serving based on the principle of Partial Reuse. FastEEP reuses existing runtime state across worker execution, GPU memory, and communication by separating reusable execution structures from the resources activated by the current EP configuration. This separation enables coordinated resource reclamation and reconfiguration while preserving costly-to-reconstruct state, allowing fast EP scaling without full instance teardown and reconstruction. Our evaluation shows that FastEEP achieves 4.5x--11.7x faster scaling than the existing vLLM-based approach across different models, enabling efficient, fine-grained scaling of MoE serving.
original_abstract.source_title: FastEEP: Fast Intra-Instance Elastic Scaling for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving

en.text: FastEEP resizes expert-parallel groups inside a running MoE serving instance by separating reusable execution state from configuration-dependent resources. Reusing worker, GPU-memory and communication state avoids destroying and rebuilding the whole instance. Across the tested models, scaling operations are 4.5–11.7 times faster than a vLLM-based approach. This is reconfiguration speed, not token-generation throughput; the design offers a systems reference for elastic sparse-model serving, with recommendation-specific workloads still requiring validation.

zh.text: FastEEP在运行中的MoE服务实例内调整专家并行组，把可复用执行状态与依赖当前配置的资源分开。复用工作进程、显存和通信状态，减少整实例销毁重建。所测模型中，扩缩容操作比基于vLLM的方案快4.5至11.7倍。该数字衡量重配置速度，不是令牌生成吞吐；其状态复用设计可供弹性稀疏模型服务参考，推荐负载仍需单独验证。

original_abstract.text: Summary-token architectures such as Kwai Summary Attention (KSA) compress distant context into learnable Summary token per chunk, and hybrid variants interleave these layers with full attention to retain exact access to the original text. In such hybrid KSA-Full architecture, the interleaving inserted summary tokens are served as a streaming flow role across different layers. Although effective, however, it also introduce some bottlenecks: (1) the different layers summary compression chunk must be same, therefore hard to reach a flexible KV Cache compression, e.g., different layer set different summary compression chunk window. (2) in the full-attention layers, the summary token introduced additional computation cost, but such layer ignore them and still pay quadratic prefilling, therefore unfriendly to the computation side. Motivated by them, we developed the KSA V2, which not only achieves a more flexible KV cache memory compression but also reduces the computation cost in Full attention layer. Specifically, we found that the summary tokens can serve two roles: the KV memory and sparse indexer.
original_abstract.source_title: Kwai Summary Attention V2 Technical Report

en.text: Kwai Summary Attention V2 addresses hybrid summary-token/full-attention models whose shared compression granularity restricts KV-cache flexibility and whose full-attention layers still incur quadratic prefill cost. Summary tokens serve both as compressed key/value memory and as sparse indexers, enabling layer-specific compression and selective access. It offers a possible design direction for long-history compression, but the reported experiments concern language models rather than CTR ranking.

zh.text: Kwai Summary Attention V2处理摘要token与全注意力混合模型的两个瓶颈：共享压缩粒度限制键值缓存的灵活性，全注意力层仍承担二次复杂度的预填充成本。摘要token同时作为压缩记忆和稀疏索引器，支持分层压缩与选择性访问。该思路可供长历史压缩参考，但论文实验针对语言模型，尚未验证CTR排序收益。

original_abstract.text: Residual connections propagate information through a network by additively accumulating layer outputs. Recently proposed alternatives, such as Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes), instead use more expressive depth aggregation mechanisms that improve language modeling performance at scale. In this work, we consider the mixing of representations over depth as a problem of storing and retrieving information across layers. Formalizing this perspective, we introduce Depth Memory (DM), a unified framework that describes the standard pre-layer-norm (PreLN) transformer, mHC, and AttnRes in terms of streams that carry representations through the network. One such stream, for example, could be an explicit memory stream that is queried to enrich the input to every layer, and whose output is subsequently written back into the memory for use by later layers. For AttnRes, this memory stream is a growing cache of explicit layer representations. For mHC, it is an expanded residual stream. Building on this view, we propose Linear Depth Memory (LDM), which formulates information retrieval across depth as a regression problem solved using recursive least squares. The resulting architecture propagates three streams across depth: the standard residual stream, a linear associative memory stream, and an inverse covariance stream. For high-throughput training and inference, we propose a hardware-aware implementation of LDM that reduces peak activation memory and memory traffic. LDM consistently achieves the lowest perplexities among PreLN, mHC and AttnRes baselines at the 400M and 1.5B parameter scales, alongside competitive zero-shot accuracy.
original_abstract.source_title: Depth Memory

en.text: Depth Memory unifies residual and cross-layer aggregation as memory retrieval. Its Linear Depth Memory variant uses recursive least squares and three depth streams, with a hardware-aware implementation that reduces overhead relative to its naive implementation. It reports the lowest perplexities among tested PreLN, mHC and AttnRes baselines at 400M and 1.5B, with competitive zero-shot accuracy. This suggests a depth-scaling direction for ranking models, but no CTR experiments establish transfer.

zh.text: Depth Memory 将残差与跨层聚合统一为记忆检索；LDM 通过递归最小二乘维护三条深度信息流，并以硬件感知实现降低其朴素实现的开销。在 400M 和 1.5B 语言模型比较中，其困惑度优于所测 PreLN、mHC 和 AttnRes，零样本准确率具有竞争力。对排序模型的启发是改善深层信息传递，尚无 CTR 迁移验证。

original_abstract.text: Sparse attention reduces the KV-cache traffic that dominates long-context LLM decoding, but practical methods largely operate at coarse granularity. Token-level selection offers finer control, yet presents two challenges: low-dimensional scoring may lose query--key structure needed for accurate ranking, while gathering scattered selected tokens can offset the resulting latency benefit. We introduce Joint Subspace Sparse Attention (JSSA) to address both challenges. For selection quality, JSSA learns a shared low-dimensional query--key subspace by minimizing token-score preservation error. We upper-bound the resulting non-convex objective with a tractable marginal objective that admits a closed-form spectral solution; direct refinement of the exact objective provides no measurable improvement in the tested settings. For execution efficiency, we develop a gather-free token-level indexed-attention kernel that supports distinct per-KV-head selections under the standard grouped-query attention (GQA) KV-cache layout. Across standard GQA, hybrid sliding-window/global attention, and Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) models, JSSA consistently remains close to full-KV accuracy while avoiding the substantial generation-length inflation and architecture-dependent failures observed with competing methods. On an NVIDIA B200 GPU, JSSA achieves up to $6.43\times$ the decoding throughput of full-KV attention at 128K context. JSSA achieves reasoning accuracy comparable to model-native DSA without model training and reaches 96--99\% of its decoding throughput even at 700B scale large models.
original_abstract.source_title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding

en.text: JSSA preserves query–key ranking information in a shared low-dimensional subspace and pairs token selection with an indexed-attention kernel that avoids gathering scattered cache entries. Tests across several attention architectures retain accuracy close to full-cache attention; on one NVIDIA B200 at 128K context with a 2,048-token KV budget, reported decoding throughput reaches up to 6.43 times the full-cache baseline. The transferable lesson is to optimize selection quality and memory access together for long histories; the experiments concern LLM decoding and do not establish recommendation serving gains.

zh.text: JSSA在共享低维子空间中保留查询与键的排序信息，并用索引注意力内核直接读取所选令牌，避免先搬运零散缓存。多种注意力架构测试中，准确率接近完整缓存注意力；在单张NVIDIA B200、128K上下文、2,048令牌KV预算条件下，解码吞吐最高达到完整缓存基线的6.43倍。对长历史建模的借鉴是共同优化筛选质量与内存访问；实验针对语言模型解码，不能直接视为推荐服务收益。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval (GR) has emerged as a strong candidate generator for sequential recommendation as language models and semantic-item identifiers have improved. However, GR is not a uniformly stronger replacement of dense retrieval (DR) in online retail candidate generation. We examine their differences on two Amazon Toys datasets under different metrics. GR leads on best relevant item value among users both methods cover, while DR leads on exact-target recall and relevant value across the ranked list. With deep analysis, we find that popularity contributes the most to GR's measured value lead. Adding the same static item value to DR in one reranking step reverses this lead and keeps recall above GR. Finally, on an industrial-scale internal e-commerce dataset with LLM-judged relevance, we show that a 14B SID-LLM still underperforms a $47\times$ smaller dense encoder.
original_abstract.source_title: Revisiting Generative vs. Dense Retrieval: A Static Value Prior Reverses the Gap

en.text: This study compares generative and dense retrieval on two Amazon Toys datasets using exact-target recall, best-item value among jointly covered users and value across the full ranked list. Their ordering changes with the metric, and adding the same static item-value prior to dense retrieval reverses the generative method’s measured best-item-value lead. A separate internal e-commerce test uses LLM-judged relevance. For recommendation scaling, it motivates matching evaluation populations, objectives and simple priors before attributing gains to larger generative models; it does not prove universal dense-retrieval superiority.

zh.text: 研究在两套Amazon Toys数据上比较生成式与稠密检索，分别看精确目标召回、双方都覆盖用户中的最佳物品价值，以及完整列表价值。方法排序随指标改变；给稠密检索加入同一静态物品价值先验后，生成式方法原有的最佳物品价值优势被反转。另有内部电商测试采用语言模型判断相关性。对推荐扩展的启示是先对齐评估人群、目标和简单先验，再归因于生成模型规模，不能推广为稠密检索普遍更强。

original_abstract.text: Large language models impose substantial memory demands and arithmetic costs during inference. Dense-to-mixture-of-experts (MoE) conversion is a model optimization technique that aims to reduce these arithmetic costs. Dense-to-MoE conversion partitions pretrained feed-forward network (FFN) neurons into experts and selects a subset for each token. Leading methods fall into two categories: analytic methods produce a converted model quickly using heuristics, while learning methods produce a model much more slowly by optimizing via gradients. Both approaches, however, fix the same active expert count, or "utilization," at every layer. We introduce Spectral-MoE, which learns to allocate a utilization budget heterogeneously across layers. Its name draws a metaphor between separating a dense FFN into experts and separating a light beam into its spectrum. Spectral-MoE consists of two distinct approaches: a static approach that uses a single per-layer scalar which is shared across tokens, and a dynamic approach which emits a per-token schedule. We demonstrate that both allocators improve performance over uniform on both the analytic-based and learning-based SOTA dense-to-MoE methods. At 25% FFN utilization, dynamic allocation reduces WikiText-2 perplexity relative to uniform by 1.04, 2.96, and 2.71 points on the learned base for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B, respectively. The corresponding reductions on the analytic base are 2.45, 6.26, and 2.17 points. On the learned base, dynamic allocation improves six-task mean accuracy over uniform by an average of 1.5, 4.2, and 3.6 percentage points across the three models at FFN utilizations of 12.5%, 25%, and 50%, respectively. These results establish per-layer expert utilization as a novel optimization axis in dense-to-MoE conversion.
original_abstract.source_title: Spectral-MoE: Heterogeneous Per-Layer Expert Utilization in Dense-to-MoE Conversion

en.text: Spectral-MoE learns unequal expert-activation allocations across layers when converting dense language models into MoEs. A static allocator shares one layer schedule across tokens; a dynamic allocator revises each token’s remaining schedule from intermediate states while conserving its total expert budget. Across three models and analytic/learned conversion bases, heterogeneous allocation improves perplexity, with dynamic allocation also improving average task accuracy. Serving speedups are not measured, and the authors’ learned-base reproduction underperforms its published baseline. CTR engineering inference: test layer-sensitive compute allocation under fixed activation budgets, then verify real serving costs. No CTR experiments are reported.

zh.text: Spectral-MoE 在稠密语言模型转换为 MoE 时，学习跨层不均匀的专家激活分配。静态方案为所有 token 共用一套分层计划；动态方案根据中间状态修订各 token 后续层的计划，同时保持每个 token 的总专家预算不变。在三种模型、解析式与学习式转换基础上，异构分配改善了困惑度，动态方案也提高了任务平均准确率。论文未测量实际服务加速，作者复现的学习式基线低于原论文成绩。对 CTR 的工程启发是在固定激活预算下测试按层分配计算，再验证实际服务成本。本文没有 CTR 实验。

original_abstract.text: Soft spectral clipping (SSC) reduces gradient singular values, but its effect depends on the gradient scale and clipping threshold. We introduce CAST (Clipping with Adaptive Scales and Thresholds), a history-adaptive extension of SSC. AdamW's previous second moment sets row and column scales. An exponential moving average of the clipped output's estimated spectral norm sets each matrix's threshold. CAST restores the original coordinates before the AdamW update. We train a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 19.08B total parameters for 83.89B tokens. CAST achieves lower training and mean validation losses than nine gradient-processing baselines, with the fewest relative gradient spikes. It reaches the best baseline's final smoothed training loss in 7.2\% fewer steps.
original_abstract.source_title: CAST: History-Adaptive Spectral Clipping for LLM Pretraining

en.text: CAST adapts soft spectral clipping before AdamW using two histories: the previous second moment sets row/column scales, and an exponential moving average of the clipped spectral norm sets each matrix’s threshold. It restores original coordinates before the optimizer update. In a single-seed MoE pretraining comparison, CAST lowers training and mean validation losses against nine gradient-processing baselines and reaches the best baseline’s final smoothed loss in fewer steps. Extra per-step work and hardware-dependent costs remain. CTR engineering inference: test history-adaptive gradient processing for unstable large-model training, reporting loss-versus-time alongside spike counts. This paper contains no CTR experiments.

zh.text: CAST 在 AdamW 更新前自适应执行软谱裁剪：用上一轮二阶矩确定梯度矩阵的行列尺度，用裁剪后谱范数的指数移动平均确定各矩阵阈值，再恢复原坐标后更新优化器。单种子 MoE 预训练对比中，其训练损失和平均验证损失低于九种梯度处理基线，并用更少步数达到最佳基线的最终平滑损失；但每步有额外开销，实际成本依赖硬件。对 CTR 的工程启发是测试基于历史的梯度处理能否改善大模型训练稳定性，同时报告损失随时间的变化与梯度尖峰数。本文没有 CTR 实验。

original_abstract.text: Memory-efficient subspace optimization has emerged as a practical approach to reducing the memory cost of LLM training while preserving optimization performance. Previous algorithms typically rely on the leading singular subspace of stochastic gradients, yet the gradient noise may dominate the subspace in later training stages and can prevent convergence. To overcome this limitation, we adopt a residual correction framework, which maintains the optimizer states in the subspace and adds the orthogonal residual gradient to the parameter update. We first integrate this scheme into momentum SGD to develop SMRC, which attains an $O(T^{-1/4})$ convergence rate for a fixed orthonormal basis, matching that of full-space momentum SGD. Our analysis introduces a subspace virtual iterate to resolve the coupling between the momentum and the residual correction. Furthermore, we extend SMRC to a multi-stage variant which periodically recomputes bases to track the evolving dominant subspace and retains the same rate. Since each basis refresh breaks the consistency of the virtual iterates, we devise a boundary correction approach that aligns them across stages. Beyond momentum SGD, we incorporate our framework into Muon and propose PMRC, which applies the matrix sign to the projected momentum. Through a weighted momentum tracking analysis that accounts for the residual gradient, we establish an $O(T^{-1/4})$ convergence rate for PMRC, which matches the rate of full-space Muon. We also design a multi-stage PMRC with periodically refreshed bases, which maintains a convergence rate of the same order. Extensive experimental results confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithms.
original_abstract.source_title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon

en.text: Low-rank optimizer states save memory, but noisy gradients can make the retained subspace miss useful update directions. SMRC for momentum SGD and PMRC for Muon keep states in the subspace and add the orthogonal residual gradient back to the update. The paper proves an O(T^(-1/4)) convergence rate matching the corresponding full-space methods, including variants that periodically refresh the basis, and reports experiments supporting effectiveness and efficiency. The abstract provides no quantitative memory or speed gains; benefits for CTR training remain unverified.

zh.text: 低秩优化器状态可以节省内存，但梯度噪声可能使保留的子空间遗漏有用的更新方向。SMRC 和 PMRC 分别面向动量 SGD 与 Muon，将优化器状态留在子空间内，并在参数更新时补回正交残差梯度。论文证明其收敛率达到 O(T^(-1/4))，与对应全空间方法同阶，周期刷新子空间基的变体也保留这一收敛阶，并报告实验支持其有效性与效率。摘要未给出具体内存或速度收益，CTR 训练中的效果仍待验证。

original_abstract.text: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under matched budgets. Prior work demonstrates that different loop visits can play different roles even when they share parameters. To probe the contributions of different loop visits, we learn separate residual coefficients in a model that applies a shared block twice, observing a smaller scale in the first visit. Fixed coefficient experiments show that reducing the first visit's scale preserves or improves performance, whereas the same reductions to the second hurt it. This asymmetry motivates us to explore asymmetric compute allocation. We propose \textbf{LatentLoop}, which compresses the first visit's sequence, retains full resolution in the second, and reallocates saved computation to increase the hidden size. We further learn how strongly the first visit updates the full sequence, and share MoE weights across visits while using separate attention parameters to accommodate their different sequence resolutions. Across 15 configurations spanning 1.3B--7B parameters, with the largest budget exceeding $10^{21}$ FLOPs, LatentLoop consistently lowers validation NLL. At a fitted NLL of 1.988, predicted compute savings are 19.0\% and 7.9\% relative to vanilla MoE and the looped baseline. It also improves average scores on nine benchmarks at all sizes in 0-shot and 5-shot settings. These results suggest asymmetric compute allocation is a promising direction for looped MoE models.
original_abstract.source_title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation

en.text: LatentLoop allocates unequal computation to two visits of a shared MoE block: the first uses a compressed sequence, the second keeps full resolution, and saved compute increases model width. It shares expert weights but separates attention parameters and learns writeback strength. Across 15 configurations from 1.3B to 7B parameters, validation NLL improves; fitted curves at NLL 1.988 predict 19.0% and 7.9% less compute than vanilla and looped MoE baselines. These are fitted language-model savings, suggesting a budget-allocation hypothesis for recommendation rather than established CTR gains.

zh.text: LatentLoop给共享MoE模块的两次循环分配不同计算量：首次压缩序列，第二次保留完整分辨率，节省的计算用于加宽模型。专家权重共享，注意力参数分开，并学习写回强度。13亿至70亿参数的15组配置中，验证负对数似然改善；在拟合损失1.988处，相对普通MoE和循环MoE预测分别省19.0%和7.9%计算。这是语言模型拟合结果，可用于提出推荐计算分配的实验假设，尚非CTR收益。

original_abstract.text: Multilingual models share capacity across languages, so adding languages can hurt performance on existing ones. Mixture-of-experts models expand this capacity with little additional per-token computation. Given this extra capacity, does adding experts reduce what each additional language costs? To answer this question, we propose a repetition-aware joint scaling law relating number of active parameters, training tokens per language, number of experts, and language coverage. Fitted on 26,300 per-language loss observations from 64 pretrained configurations, our law reduces prediction error on held-out configurations by 28% relative to the strongest evaluated baseline. At matched number of active parameters and training tokens per language, 32 experts reduce the loss penalty of expanding from 12 to 200 languages by 83% compared with a dense model. Our law further shows that broader language coverage favors more experts across a wider range of compute budgets, guiding capacity allocation as multilingual models scale.
original_abstract.source_title: Scaling Multilingual Mixture-of-Experts: How Language Coverage Changes Capacity and Compute Allocation

en.text: This study fits a repetition-aware scaling law linking active parameters, per-language training tokens, expert count, and language coverage. Across controlled multilingual pretraining configurations, extra experts reduce the penalty of broader coverage when active capacity and tokens per language are matched. Broader coverage also shifts the modeled capacity allocation toward experts, yet preserving average quality can still leave individual languages worse off. Conclusions are bounded by the studied Top-1 architecture and training regime; logical compute excludes hardware overheads. CTR engineering inference: allocate capacity across traffic domains while checking slice-level regressions and data repetition. These are multilingual language-model results, not CTR experiments.

zh.text: 研究建立了考虑数据重复的扩展定律，将激活参数量、每种语言的训练 token 数、专家数和语言覆盖范围联系起来。在匹配激活容量及每语言训练量的受控预训练中，增加专家能缓解扩大语言覆盖造成的损失；模型推算的容量分配也更偏向专家。但恢复平均质量并不保证每种语言都不退步。结论受所测 Top-1 架构和训练配置限制，逻辑计算量不包含硬件开销。对 CTR 的工程启发是：跨流量域分配容量时，同时检查分域退步和数据重复。本文是多语言建模研究，没有 CTR 实验。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models activate only a few experts per token, yet all expert weights must be stored. Mixed-precision quantization reduces this storage cost by assigning higher bit-widths to sensitive experts and lower bit-widths to resilient ones, but expert rankings alone do not determine how strongly to weight their errors. To address this gap, we propose NatScale, a contrast-calibrated allocation framework for mixed-precision MoE quantization. It uses a model-specific power transformation to calibrate gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings. We jointly evaluate each expert's gate, up and down configurations to estimate its output error. We then combine these errors and calibrated weights with an existing prior based on weight spectra, variance and precision decay to select configurations under a storage budget. Across three models, NatScale achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and the highest top-token agreement in all nine settings against five allocation baselines. It also yields the lowest perplexity in seven settings. These findings highlight the importance of objective-aware precision allocation.
original_abstract.source_title: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization

en.text: NatScale calibrates the contrast of gradient-based expert importance weights while preserving their ordering, then allocates mixed precision under a storage budget using joint gate/up/down error estimates. Across three MoE models and nine settings it gives the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and highest top-token agreement against five allocation baselines, and the lowest perplexity in seven settings. Recommendation-model benefits remain untested.

zh.text: 给专家按重要性排序，还不足以确定不同专家的量化误差应相差多少。NatScale在保持排序的同时校准权重差距，联合估计专家各投影的误差，并在存储预算内分配精度。在三个MoE模型、九组设置中，相对五种分配基线均取得最低分布偏差和最高首选词元一致率，七组困惑度最低；推荐模型收益尚待验证。

original_abstract.text: Tabular foundation models enable in-context learning by predicting unseen observations from a labeled support table without task-specific parameter updates. Despite recent advances, most existing approaches rely on dense architectures that apply the same transformations across features and datasets. We introduce OrionMoE-Small-v1.0, a compact tabular foundation model that combines distribution-aware representations with dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts computation. Built on a dual-axis transformer architecture, OrionMoE-Small selectively activates experts with routing decisions informed by both individual cell representations and the broader dataset context. This design enables adaptive allocation of computation across heterogeneous tabular problems while retaining a shared computational pathway across tasks. The model is pretrained entirely on synthetic classification tasks generated from a structured causal prior and performs downstream prediction without gradient-based adaptation. Experiments across multiple tabular benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance against substantially larger foundation models, with particularly strong results on small-context and high-dimensional datasets. Further analysis reveals favorable relative performance under class imbalance and highlights the importance of feature composition.
original_abstract.source_title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning

en.text: OrionMoE-Small-v1.0 combines distribution-aware representations with dataset-conditioned sparse expert computation in a dual-axis tabular Transformer. The revised abstract describes routing as conditioned on individual cell representations and the wider dataset context, removing the earlier feature-axis-only wording. Synthetic-task pretraining enables prediction from labeled support tables without task-specific gradient updates, with competitive reported results against larger tabular foundation models. The revision corrects the mechanism description; it does not establish new recommendation results or new performance gains.

zh.text: OrionMoE-Small-v1.0 在双轴表格 Transformer 中结合分布感知表示与数据集相关的稀疏专家计算。新版摘要把路由依据明确为单元格表示和整体数据集上下文，删除了原先沿特征轴选择专家的表述。模型通过合成任务预训练，无需任务级梯度更新即可根据带标签的支持表预测，作者报告与更大表格基座模型具有竞争力的结果。本次是机制说明更正，不代表新增推荐实验或新的性能收益。

original_abstract.text: The scaling relationship of compute and performance for language models (LMs) has been extensively studied; more recently, models are being designed to scale memory use, as well. In particular, adding embeddings for n-grams scales memory separately from compute use, because each pass only processes individual embedding rows, which are much smaller than the storage used for the whole embedding table. However, existing methods train embeddings from scratch, which needs expensive GPU memory for fast reading and writing. Meanwhile, the ordinary memory of the host system is cheap and underutilized by these training methods. To scale on host memory, we introduce COUNT (Counting Offline Unlocks N-gram Transformers), which builds n-gram embeddings without adding learned parameters by storing precomputed n-gram counts on host. We use the corpus frequencies to weight together the LM's own unembeddings of the next tokens most often following the current n-gram history. At a fixed compute budget, COUNT can be added as an additional input embedding for pretraining 1B-parameter LMs to improve validation loss as much as an LM with 57% more compute. If GPU memory is limited, using COUNT to let backbone parameters fill GPU memory gives better performance than splitting memory with additional learned n-gram embeddings. Beyond efficiency, COUNT allows switching in a different table of n-gram counts from a domain-specific corpus at inference time to adapt to a new task without any training.
original_abstract.source_title: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation

en.text: COUNT stores precomputed n-gram counts in host memory and uses those frequencies to combine the language model’s output embeddings into additional input embeddings, without a separately learned n-gram table. In 1B-parameter pretraining, the authors report validation-loss gains comparable to spending 57% more estimated training compute on the baseline; changing count tables also enables training-free domain adaptation. Separating cheap stored statistics from active computation is relevant to memory-heavy recommendation designs, but the reported gains are language-model results, not CTR measurements.

zh.text: COUNT把预计算的n元词组计数放在主机内存，用频率加权语言模型的输出嵌入，构造额外输入嵌入，无需另学一张n元词组嵌入表。在10亿参数语言模型预训练中，作者报告的验证损失改善相当于基线多用57%估算训练计算量；替换计数表还能免训练适配领域。把低成本存储统计与实际计算分离，可为推荐的大容量记忆设计提供借鉴，但这些收益来自语言模型，未经CTR验证。

original_abstract.text: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.
original_abstract.source_title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models

en.text: ReaDy supplies a speculative drafter with position-specific context retrieved from the recurrent states of a hybrid linear-attention target model. Learned queries and a lightweight residual state reader complement ordinary hidden features; low-rank reads and fused operators limit additional I/O and computation. On seven benchmarks with Qwen3.8-27B on one NVIDIA B200, the authors report higher throughput and more output tokens per verification round than pretrained DSpark. This suggests reusing compressed recurrent memory as an active information source for generation, not just a passive cache; it assumes access to suitable hybrid-model states and does not demonstrate recommendation gains.

zh.text: ReaDy让推测解码的草稿模型按预测位置，从混合线性注意力模型的循环状态中读取额外上下文。它用可学习查询和轻量残差读取器补充普通隐藏特征，并以低秩读取和融合算子控制额外计算与I/O。在单张NVIDIA B200上运行Qwen3.8-27B的七项测试中，作者报告其吞吐量与每轮验证输出的令牌数均优于预训练DSpark。可借鉴的是主动复用压缩循环记忆，但需要可读取的混合模型状态，尚无推荐收益证据。

original_abstract.text: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. At two bits, errors in this representation perturb both attention matching and value readout, with effects that depend on error direction and reconstruction scale. We introduce RoLaQ (Rotation-calibrated Latent Quantization), an offline method for joint rotation and range calibration. RoLaQ refines a shared rotation within subspaces defined by the frozen key and value projections, and jointly learns quantization ranges whose thresholds and reconstruction gains are coupled to control the shared signal's response. Prediction matching and attention-output supervision guide calibration with model weights frozen. Across three MLA models and six benchmarks, RoLaQ achieves the highest average accuracy among the compared 2-bit methods both without and with token protection. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, an SGLang implementation provides 3.96 times the BF16 KV capacity under the same memory budget and 2.51 times its decode throughput with 256K input tokens.
original_abstract.source_title: RoLaQ: Joint Rotation and Range Calibration for 2-Bit KV Caches in Multi-Head Latent Attention

en.text: RoLaQ jointly calibrates rotations and quantization ranges for the shared content latent in multi-head latent attention, using frozen key/value projections and teacher predictions plus attention outputs. It achieves the highest six-benchmark average among compared 2-bit methods across three MLA models. Only content latents are quantized; positional keys remain BF16, with optional protected tokens. DeepSeek-V2-Lite serving tests improve long-context capacity and throughput, but short-context overhead can outweigh savings and measurements cover one A100 setup. CTR engineering inference: calibrate compressed shared representations against every downstream consumer and benchmark realistic sequence lengths. The paper evaluates language models, not CTR experiments.

zh.text: RoLaQ 利用冻结的 key/value 投影，以及教师预测和注意力输出，联合校准多头潜在注意力共享内容表示的旋转与量化范围。在三种 MLA 模型中，它取得所比较 2-bit 方法里最高的六项基准平均分。量化仅针对内容表示，位置 key 仍为 BF16，也可保护部分 token。DeepSeek-V2-Lite 服务实验提升了长上下文容量与吞吐，但短上下文的量化开销可能抵消收益，服务测试仅覆盖一种 A100 配置。对 CTR 的工程启发是：共享表示压缩应同时校准所有下游用途，并按实际序列长度测试。本文评估语言模型，没有 CTR 实验。
